sga5.french: Repair032 is public as a bundled audit-support artifact on record 20822648, but it is not a completed or certified SGA5 edition. The latest local SGA5 control package is `SGA5_FullAudit_WebDrop_p001_p253_certified_staged_p254_p484_20260626.zip` under manifest `20260626_sga5_fullaudit_webdrop_p253_staged_p254_p484.json`. It preserves the active French workpass TeX/PDF/log, the controlling CERT_LOG and AGENT_SCORECARD ledgers, method/status notes, source-witness crops/images, file inventory, and checksums. The controlling ledger rows reach p253; p254-p484 are staged source witnesses only, not promoted/certified pages. Around the current endpoint, p250-p253 close Expose V and open Expose VI: p250 finishes Theorem A.3/QED and Expose V, p251 opens Expose VI, p252 records the V-to-VI bridge plus Props. 1.1.2/1.1.3 opening, and p253 closes Prop. 1.1.3 proof (kernel via MLAR, m_r(K'), and gluing) while opening section 1.1.4. Diagrams remain tallied D001-D142; p253 has no diagram. D140 keeps its earlier recorded layout simplification: source-verified mathematical labels and bidegree content, but the TeX collapses distinct source `O` and `alpha` verticals. This is live French workpass/source-audit evidence only: not complete SGA5, not synchronized English, not global source-faithfulness certification, and not a critical edition. Local ledger words such as certified or complete mean page-local workpass status only. Agents/workflows are finders and repair aids, not certifiers; substantial source reconciliation, English synchronization, and independent validation remain open. The latest observed sga5_fr_workpass.log writes a 307-page PDF and the fatal-error scan is clean, but compile-clean TeX can still be mathematically wrong. This is strong repair evidence, not closure. It proves both diagram errors and prose/symbol-level errors exist in older SGA5 surfaces, and old complete labels mean only that a listed repair batch finished, not that SGA5 is source-faithful. Lean material is tracked as useful Lean 4 / mathlib-style candidate additions inspired by the archive, not as proof, transcription/translation audit, source-fidelity evidence, or certification of scanned editions.

Public pages should describe remaining dense-region and diagram work instead of relying on optimistic legacy filenames.
